chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashshab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh, from Amr ibn Jumi', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever does not ask God, Mighty and Majestic, of His grace has indeed become poor.

key_terms.افتقر: To become poor/destitute — spiritual poverty from neglecting supplication
key_terms.فضل: Grace, bounty, favor — God's freely given gifts beyond mere requital

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the consequence of not supplicating to God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that supplication to God is not merely a devotional act but a spiritual necessity. One who abstains from asking God for His grace and bounty impoverishes himself spiritually, cutting himself off from the divine source of all provision. This hadith was transmitted in the context of Imam al-Sadiq's teachings on the virtues and urgency of du'a, emphasizing that God's bounty is inexhaustible and that withholding one's supplication is an act of spiritual deprivation.
